newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes softened by imports and NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes softened by imports and NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes fell Friday amid profit-taking in energy futures and talk that refiners bought foreign alternatives to Alaskan crude, traders said.
Tosco on Thursday bought a 360,000-barrel cargo of Cano Limon for $3.10 a barrel under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, the American benchmark grade, traders said.
Some players thought Tosco paid too high a price for the grade, which typically costs minus $4.00.
NYMEX crude oil for June fell 31 cents a barrel to $19.60.

Traders could not say if Ecopetrol, Colombia's state-owned oil company, had announced the winners of two cargoes of Cusiana, a gasoline-rich crude, which was bid $1.40-45 under WTI, with offers seen minus $1.20, traders said.
The grade is sold to U.S. Gulf Coast refiners more often than to West Coast players, traders said.
One trader said he heard Tosco and Texaco, two West Coast refiners who can run Cusiana, had failed to win the cargoes.
Imports put pressure on California grades. The widening Alaska North Slope (ANS) discount lowered demand for Line 63, a substitute grade which is blended from California crudes.
Traders did not discuss ANS Friday, but a major producer offered at $1.15 under WTI, 12 cents more expensive than a deal done earlier this week at minus $1.37.
Meanwhile, Buena Vista, a component of 63, was lowered on the postings market Friday, with Texaco dropping its price 75 cents to $15.95. That follows Chevron's 50-cent decrease to $16.20 a barrel.
Traders said Thursday's weak interest in the U.S. government's Elk Hills crude auction reflected the heavy volumes of foreign crude on the West Coast.
Only 11,000 barrels of the available 16,000 light barrels were requested, traders said.
"It would appear that people can't give it away," one trader said.
Kern River, a California heavy grade, eased slightly after Texaco lowered its posted price for the grade Friday.
